bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding Your Teacher Salary Victoria: From Hourly to Annual

If you're a teacher in Victoria, you may be paid an hourly rate under an award or enterprise agreement. Converting that rate to an annual salary helps you compare job offers or plan your budget. The formula is simple: multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then by 52 weeks. This article explains the calculation, including casual loading, superannuation, and tax, using the latest Fair Work and ATO figures.

### The Formula: Hourly Rate × Hours × 52

For a full-time teacher working a standard 38-hour week, your annual gross pay is:

**Annual gross = hourly rate × 38 × 52**

For example, if your hourly rate is $40.00:
- Weekly pay: $40.00 × 38 = $1,520.00
- Fortnightly pay: $1,520.00 × 2 = $3,040.00
- Annual gross: $1,520.00 × 52 = $79,040.00

If you work a different number of hours per week, adjust the formula accordingly. The timesheet on this site does the calculation for you – just enter your base hourly rate and the hours you work.

### Casual Loading and Superannuation

Many teachers are employed casually, which means you receive a 25% loading on top of your base rate. On our [timesheet](/), you enter the base rate and check the casual loading box; the calculator adds 25% automatically. **Do not enter a rate that already includes casual loading.**

For a casual teacher with a base rate of $40.00:
- Casual rate: $40.00 + 25% = $50.00 per hour
- Weekly pay (38 hours): $50.00 × 38 = $1,900.00
- Annual gross: $1,900.00 × 52 = $98,800.00

Superannuation is paid on top of your ordinary earnings. The super guarantee is 12% of your gross pay, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. So if your annual gross is $79,040, your employer pays an extra $9,484.80 into your super account. This is not deducted from your pay – it's additional.

### Tax and Take-Home Pay

Your take-home pay depends on the 2026–27 resident tax rates and the Medicare levy. For a full-time teacher earning $79,040 annually:
- Tax-free threshold: $0 – $18,200
- 15% on $18,201 – $45,000: $4,020
- 30% on $45,001 – $135,000: $10,212 (on $34,040)
- Total tax: $14,232
- Medicare levy (2%): $1,580.80
- Total deductions: $15,812.80
- Annual take-home: $63,227.20
- Fortnightly take-home: $63,227.20 ÷ 26 ≈ $2,431.82

This is an estimate. It assumes no HELP debt, no Medicare levy surcharge, and no salary sacrifice. Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) guide for more details.

### Average Pay Comparisons

The Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) reports average full-time ordinary time earnings in Victoria as $2,041.10 per week (May 2026). That's about $106,137 annually. However, this is an average across all occupations, not specifically for teachers. Your teacher salary Victoria may be higher or lower depending on your experience, school sector, and award. See our [average pay](/topics/average-pay) page for more data.

### National Minimum Wage and Award Rates

The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. Casual workers get $33.05 per hour including 25% loading. Most teachers are covered by awards or enterprise agreements that pay above the minimum. The Fair Work Ombudsman provides [pay guides](/blog) for each industry. Check your specific award to find your correct rate.

### Fortnightly Pay

Many Victorian teachers are paid fortnightly. To find your fortnightly gross, multiply your weekly pay by 2. For the $40/hour example: $1,520 × 2 = $3,040. After tax and Medicare, your fortnightly take-home is roughly $2,431.82.

### Using the Timesheet

Our [timesheet](/) is the easiest way to convert your hourly rate to annual, fortnightly, and weekly figures. Enter your base hourly rate, select your hours per week (default 38), and check the casual loading box if applicable. The calculator shows gross pay, super, and an estimate of tax and take-home. Remember: super is paid on top, and tax is based on the 2026–27 resident scale.

### Important Notes

- The formula assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice.
- Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base.
- Tax uses the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here.
- This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

For more detailed information, explore our [reference tables](/data) and guides on [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging), [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading), and [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion).
